title: Length Bias Exploitation: Do Language Models Learn to Write Longer Answers to Satisfy Overseers?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly tests a concrete, measurable instance of reward hacking. Length bias is well-documented and this experiment would show whether models actively exploit it during oversight training. Immediately relevant to RLHF safety.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Measuring output length over training is trivial. Training under oversight requires existing RLHF or weak-to-strong setup, but the measurement itself is simple. Length is an easy metric for beginners to track.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Single clear hypothesis: do outputs get longer without quality improvement? Single metric (length vs. quality over training steps). Very focused deliverable. Fits well within 30 hours.
